Posted by Richard Cowan
October 4, 2005

(MarijuanaNews note: Steve Tuck is filing for an emergency stay of his departure order, now set for Thursday, October 6, 2005, at One PM. At that time he is to report to the Canadian border services to be returned to the US. If he is taken into federal custody his life will be in great danger, but Canadas honor will have been disgraced.  

I have been fighting the insanity of the war on cannabis users for many years, but I have never encountered a story more worthy of Kafka's talents than Canada's betrayal of Steve Tuck and its own principles.   

I have been writing about the cases of the American medical refugee's since they were first arrested, and I have always believed that justice would ultimately prevail for them here.
See
 Kubby and Tuck Freed After Being Held Hellish Conditions. Marc Emery Posts Bail. MarijuanaNews Bulletin

However, I now feel grief for Canada. I hope that I do not have more reason to feel grief for Steve. He has already suffered more than anyone should have to endure. 

When you read the summary of Steves story below, which is the basis of his last minute appeal, you will understand why I am so appalled.

Please contact the officials listed at the bottom of this page.)

From Steve Tucks Appeal

Summary Of The Four Points In My Appeal.

Point One:
The RCMP , working with agents of the US Drug Enforcement Administration in Canada, repeatedly violated my rights and the rights of several Canadians, and  lied to the Canadian Border Service Agency about what happen in order to prevent the approval of a Pre-Removal Risk Assessment prior to my being delivered into US Federal Custody.  (Supported by sworn affidavits by Canadian citizens.)

Point Two:
My need for medical cannabis is the central point in my seeking the protection of Canada. However, from the beginning Immigration Canada has insisted that it would only accept the testimony of a medical expert of its own choosing, and yet it has consistently refused to provide a specialist to examine me. Nonetheless, they keep saying that I have not proven that I need cannabis.

Point Three:
The Canadian government arranged for me to bring a large quantity of cannabis seeds into Canada from the US and accepted these seeds for its medical marijuana program, but now seeks to have me punished for the process that produced these seeds.

Point Four:
I have said repeatedly that I am willing to return to the US to stand trial on state charges, and only fear being charged by the Federal government, which would not allow me to use medical cannabis while I was awaiting trial, or even to mention my need for medical cannabis when I stood trial on any federal charges. The Board said this fear was speculative, but there is clear evidence that the US federal government has been active in my case in Canada.

Explanation Of These Four Points.

Explanation of Point One:
The RCMP , working with agents of the US Drug Enforcement Administration in Canada, repeatedly violated my rights and the rights of several Canadians, and  lied to the Canadian Border Service Agency about what happen in order to prevent the approval of a Pre-Removal Risk Assessment prior to my being delivered into US Federal Custody.

In July of last year (2004), while I was working on a large mining claim on Ashlu Creek near Squamish, I was illegally detained by the RCMP. The RCMP acknowledged the role of the DEA in instigating the raids and attempting to have me kidnapped i. e. illegally taken into custody and then taken to the US.

I did not mention these facts in my PRRA, because under the PRRA rules, I was only allowed to introduce facts subsequent to the rejection of my first court appeal, and I did not know that these repeated violations of my rights and those of a number of Canadian citizens had been twisted into a reason to deny my request for a PRRA.

Consequently, I was astonished when Karl Chan, the CBSA Enforcement Officer who interviewed me (i. e. told me that my PRRA request had been rejected) said that the RCMP had been to Squamish with the DEA and had arrested me because I had been growing cannabis.

In other words, the CBSA was aware that the DEA was involved in my case in Canada at the same time that the CBSA was saying in its rejection of my PRRA application that there is insufficient evidence that to indicate that the US federal government is seeking the applicant

What really happened at Ashlu Creek:

In the Spring of last year, while exploring for mineralization on a mining property, I found that there was a large outdoor marijuana grow op being run by what appeared to be an Eastern European organized crime group. We were in the process of claiming this area, so I politely asked them to move off of our property, for obvious reasons. (I have a BC mining license.)

They then began shooting at our buildings, and otherwise placing our lives and property at risk. At that point, I began complaining to the local police and told them where to find the grow op. We also took ore samples to the Squamish RCMP offices, to prove that we were there on mining business. They showed no interest.
(MarijuanaNews note: For those in the movement who think that all growers are somehow all good guys, get a grip! Thugs are not sanctified by growing cannabis.) 

However, when I repeatedly called 911 to report these crimes of violence, the police were derisive or indifferent and said that they did not have the manpower to respond to my complaints of trespassing by armed men, being shot at, assaulted by men on dirt bikes, and having our property vandalized and/or stolen.

Instead, the RCMP came onto our property in force several times without any warrants or probable cause and held me and my associates, Canadian citizens, at gun point. We never had guns, and at no time were we growing any cannabis, which they always claimed to be seeking.

I even offered to show them the mine tunnels, so that they could see that we were not growing underground, but they refused to go into the mines claiming that would be too dangerous. We tried to tell them where to find the large grow op, but they wanted to search our property instead.

One raid occurred on July 17, 2004, when one of the growers on a dirt bike attempted to run over one of our workers and was injured when our man defended himself. Again, the RCMP showed no interested in the gangsters, but a S.W.A.T. team with perhaps 6 to 8 officers in full gear were then sent up to the mining camp to arrest me, even though I was at least one hundred yards away from the incident, I am a disabled veteran, and I was not armed, and I never been charged with any crime while I have been in Canada. All that I had done was repeatedly call them and report crimes that they said they lacked the manpower to investigate.

Altogether, they had an army of approximately 30 heavily armed men and even had a motor home, which they used as a command center. They made me lie face down in a mud puddle for an extended period with an automatic weapon cocked and pointed at my head.

They also held others on our staff and a visitor at gunpoint and even attempted to intimidate the visitor, a slightly built woman from Vancouver, by cocking their rifles while holding her. (I am not using the name of the woman in question in this public document because she fears police retaliation, but she is providing a sworn affidavit confirming her account.)

They also held my associate James Henderson, a young Canadian film maker, (along with the woman) at gunpoint by the side of the road for approximately three hours without cause. (James is also providing a sworn affidavit confirming what happened.)

This raid included the presence of a pair of detectives from what one identified as the major crime squad, so they were clearly able to determine the facts if they had wanted to.

I was taken into custody by the Squamish RCMP without being charged with any crime and was held overnight in the Squamish jail. Being deprived of cannabis, I was unable to urinate and had to be taken to the hospital in Squamish to be catheterized. At that time the doctor expressed his concern that my kidneys might be permanently damaged. I was ill for weeks afterwards and had to take antibiotics for the resulting infection.

How is it that the CBSA can know that I was arrested there, but claim not to know that I had to be hospitalized and catheterized as a result of being denied access to cannabis because of that illegal arrest?

Why was I told by a member of the Squamish RCMP that the DEA had warrants for my arrest, but the CBSA claims there is insufficient evidence that to indicate that the US federal government is seeking the applicant??

The Squamish RCMP was acting in collusion with the DEA and said that I was going to be taken to the border and turned over to US authorities. They had to release me when they were informed by my (then) attorney that my removal order was under a stay and they would be guilty of kidnapping me if they took me to the border against my will.

It would seem to me that they were already guilty of kidnapping me and nearly causing me irreparable harm by arresting me under false pretenses and holding me without valid charges in their jail at the behest of the DEA.
See
 Kubby and Tuck Allowed to Appeal Denial of Refugee Status. Canadian Law Enforcement Violates The Law With Multiple Attacks On Tuck. Hayes Simply Takes Leave.

James Henderson will testify: After putting us off about Steve's whereabouts for about eight hours, at about 1AM Cnst. Jeff Karran (husband of RCMP officer Miriam Karran to whom Tuck had complained about the growers) emerged and told (the woman visitor) and me that Steve was going back to America and there wasn't anything we could do about it.

On the next raid, they attempted to get us evicted from the property, even though we were there legally with the authorization of the agent for the corporation that owned some of the claims. Again we were held at gunpoint for no reason, but they had to leave when we demonstrated that we were legally entitled to be there.

Finally, on August 25th our worker who had been attacked by the gangster on the dirt-bike and I went into North Vancouver, to appear in court for the charges supposedly laid as a result of the events on July 17th, even though the police knew I was not involved in any way.

When we went to court we found that in fact no charges had been laid, so we then returned to the mining camp. In our absence, a large contingent of heavily armed RCMP had gone to the camp without any warrant or probable cause and removed the lock from the gate and had held my associate James Henderson at gunpoint again with automatic weapons cocked.

They had previously had every opportunity to search the property for plants, and this raid occurred on the very day that the Crown had declined to bring charges. Nonetheless, they stayed on the property for three days.

Finally, after we once again told them where to find the huge grow op, they did raid it a few days later, and 1,300 plants were seized and two armed men were arrested. 
(It should be noted that they never returned the lock that they illegally removed from the gate and the property suffered hundreds of thousands of dollars damage from the vandalism which they never investigated.)

The news article in the September 3, 2004, Squamish Chief confirms the fact that I had been complaining for months, but does not explain why the RCMP kept raiding us and not the grow op. From the September 3, 2004, Squamish Chief:

(Cpl.  Dave) Ritchie said complaints originating from the Ashlu area started to come into his office in March.

"We had reports of people protecting the area in an aggressive way," Ritchie said.

The police started to monitor the area after the complaints started to come in.

Ritchie said the pot bust and the incident involving the miners are totally separate and unrelated matters.  He noted that the marijuana was not growing on the mine property.
(We did claim the property on which they were growing and a record of this is available online.)
See ashlumines.com

Why would the Squamish RCMP violate my rights repeatedly and not investigate crimes of violence committed by the gangsters with a very large marijuana grow operation?

Why was the DEA/RCMP seeking to have us removed from a mining property after they had failed to find any evidence of wrong-doing of any kind on our part?

Why would the RCMP act in collusion with the DEA to violate my rights on Canadian soil and yet the CBSA claim that there is no evidence that my rights would be violated if I were forced to return to the US?

If the DEA will violate my rights while I am in Canada, how can anyone claim that there is no risk that they will violate my rights when I am completely at their mercy in the US?

Does the DEA only violate Americans rights when they are in Canada under the protection of a Canadian court order?

It is clear that the PRRA process itself was fraudulently contaminated by the RCMP/DEA/CBSA. False evidence that I was given no opportunity to refute was used to turn repeated violations of Canadian law and my rights into a reason for preventing an honest assessment of the risks that I would face if I was forced to return to the US.

I would not even know that this had happened had Mr. Chan not used it as an excuse to justify this fraudulent process.

Explanation of Point Two:
My medical condition and need for cannabis.

My need for medical cannabis is the central point in my seeking the protection of Canada, because I would suffer extreme pain and might not survive due process if I were deprived of cannabis while being held on bail awaiting trial. (As noted above, while I was detained in Squamish and deprived of cannabis, I was unable to urinate and this damaged my kidneys.)

However, from the beginning Immigration Canada has insisted that it would only accept the testimony of a medical expert of its own choosing, and yet it has consistently refused to provide a specialist to examine me. This point was raised repeatedly in the Refugee hearings, as is reflected in the record. I offered voluminous medical records from the United States, but that was not acceptable.

Nonetheless, in the rejection of my PRRA, J. Mensick said, With respect to the issue of his medical condition, I find the applicant has provided insufficient medical evidence that marijuana is required in the course of his treatment.  Whether this pain and condition requires treatment with marijuana has not been established by the applicant, beyond his personal assertions

In other words, the refusal by Immigration Canada to provide a medical expert to examine me is being twisted into a claim that I have provided insufficient medical evidence that marijuana is required

Inasmuch as Canada has recognized that persons in need of medical cannabis have a fundamental right to have it, it would seem that Immigration Canada is obstructing justice by using its own refusal to appoint a medical specialist to examine me as the basis for denying the protection of Canada.  

I think that Immigration Canada refused to provide its own medical expert to examine me because the specialist that they chose to examine my fellow refugee, Steven Kubby, actually confirmed Kubby's medical condition and his need for cannabis. Consequently, they avoided this problem in my case by refusing to look at the facts and then trying to place the burden on me, despite my repeated requests to be examined by a specialist.
(MarijuanaNews note: Typically, Immigration Canada simply ignored their own specialist's testimony about Kubby. When Michele Kubby referred to him as the government's doctor' the Crown's attorney objected that he was not employed by the government, which was literally true, of course, but completely misleading.)
See
 A Critique of the Kubby Refugee Ruling: What Is It About Dead That You Don't Understand?
and links

Explanation of Point Three:
The Canadian government arranged for me to bring a large quantity of cannabis seeds into Canada from the US and accepted these seeds for its medical marijuana program, but now seeks to have me punished for the process that produced these seeds.
(MarijuanaNews note: I first wrote about this in 2003.)
See
 Three Separate Canadian Stories May 13, 2003. You Connect The Dots. Steve Tucks Hearings; Canadian Justice Minister Grovels Toward Gomorrah, DC That Is. And A Subtle Twist In The Party Line.

Canada says that I must return to California to face trial for growing medical cannabis in California. However, on my first trip to Canada, Health Canada was more than willing to help me bring a very large quantity of cannabis seeds across the border, and accept them as my gift. (I have degrees in Botany and Horticulture.) These seeds had been produced by the very actions for which Canada now says I must stand trial in the US.

These seeds were accepted by Canada in order to start its medical cannabis production, but the government of Canada is now willing to have me go to prison and suffer and die because I am denied access to the medicine they were willing to break international law to obtain.
(MarijuanaNews note: HC sort of denies this. They say that seeds used to grow Health Canada's supply of marihuana had already been seized by law enforcement authorities when the decision was made to use them for the government contract to cultivate marihuana for medical purposes. Health Canada did not receive or accept seeds donated by individuals. Seeds were transferred under legal authorities through Health Canada to Prairie Plant Systems Inc for use in research and development.

Of course, that is sort of bureaucratically true. They describe the way that Canada took control of the seeds. Stop and think about HC's statement that they used seeds already seized by law enforcement. How could anyone begin a medical cannabis program with seeds of such dubious origin. They would have no way of knowing what they were really growing.

As it happens, both Marc Emery and I saw the box before Steve sent it.)

Canada will not even determine whether the US Federal government will seek to prosecute me for bringing the seeds to Canada at the same time that it seeking to extradite three Canadians to the US for sending seeds there. Is that justice?

In its refusal to grant me a Pre-Removal Risk Assessment, the government of Canada will not even consider the possibility that a vindictive US government might seek to prosecute me for this action by the Canadian government.

Explanation of Point Four:
I have said repeatedly that I am willing to return to the US to stand trial on state charges, and only fear being charged by the Federal government, which would not allow me to use medical cannabis while I was awaiting trial, or even to mention my need for medical cannabis when I stood trial on any federal charges. The Board said this fear was speculative, but there is clear evidence that the US federal government has been active in my case in Canada.

From the beginning, I have made clear that I was not fleeing due process in the United States. I did not come to Canada with the intention of seeking asylum. I left Humboldt County because I was in fear of my life, after I was warned that certain corrupt police officers and prosecutors intended to jail me without proper medication.

In my refugee hearings, the government's own witness, Sergeant Hansen, a narc who had vandalized my home (according to the testimony, in the hearing transcript, of a private detective who is accepted as an expert witness in California courts) and against whom I had brought charges, said that I would not be allowed to use cannabis or morphine while in the county jail.
See
 Tuck Refugee Hearings End. The Facts Put Canada In Awkward Position. Catching A Nark In A Lie? Imagine That! News and Analysis by Richard Cowan.

He said that only if they decided I was suffering too much they would consider moving me to a hospital where I would be given morphine, but no cannabis. Inasmuch as the same people who had vandalized my home would have had the power of life and (a very painful) death over me, I was advised by my attorney to flee for my life.

Sadly, there is strong reason to believe that my fear was more than justified. In 2003, a close friend and fellow medical marijuana activist, Christopher Robert Giauque, disappeared. Previously, I had witnessed Chris kidnapped by local police in Humboldt. That is, the police grabbed Chris and threw him into a police car in broad daylight without arresting him or reading him his rights and sped away. This was in front of the County Court House! 

However, there were no witnesses the last time. His family thinks that he was kidnapped and murdered, probably by organized crime elements in collusion with corrupt elements in law enforcement that saw the medical marijuana movement as a threat to their black market business. Chris and I were teaching patients to grow their own medicine, so they would not be dependent on the black market. As is the case in many areas, organized crime has been protected by corrupt elements in the police. That is why I felt that my own life would be in danger, and I could not count on due process much less the protection of the state at that time. 

Subsequently, a new District Attorney (county prosecutor) was elected in Humboldt, and I concluded that it would be safe to return there and seek due process. I have never been afraid of facing trial for growing medical cannabis in Humboldt County.

However, I could still be prosecuted under US federal laws for both cannabis related activities and for interstate flight to avoid prosecution, so I asked in my PRAA application, Shouldn't any pre-removal risk assessment necessarily involve determining whether I would risk  federal prosecution if I am forced to return to the US?

Mensick's rejection of my PRRA says that the above mentioned Sargeant (sic) Hansen, of the Humboldt Law Enforcement (sic) indicated (?) that law enforcement, including the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), are overwhelmed by the number of marijuana grow operations in the state and generally will only be involved in large grow operations that have 1,000 or more plants.

First, as the record shows, we pointed out at the time that Hansen is not an authority on federal policies, so, even if he were a credible witness, his claims are meaningless.

Second, Mensick ignores the following statement in my PRRA application:

Last month, Steve McWilliams, a San Diego medical marijuana patient/activist committed suicide rather than face federal prison. His case involved just 25 plants, but he was denied access to medical marijuana while waiting to see if the Raich case would prevent him from being sent to prison, for only six months, where he knew he would suffer even more.
See
 The Murder of Steve McWilliams An Indictment, Not An Obituary. The Absurdity of Evil. Condolences from NORML.

This is not a unique case. Another medical marijuana activist, B. E. Smith, was sentenced to 27 months in Federal prison for growing only 87 plants in 1999, four years before Hansen said that the federal government was too busy to go after small growers.
See
Smith Sentenced to 27 Months In Federal Prison For 87 Medical Marijuana Plants:
Judge Cites Smith's "Disdain For Federal Law" What Is The Definition Of A "Political Prisoner?"

In other words, there is a well established pattern that shows that any outspoken advocate of medical marijuana runs the risk of Federal prosecution no matter how few plants he or she may have been accused of growing. I could still be in Humboldt to this day if I had not been an outspoken patient advocate (and had been willing to bribe a few corrupt narcs.) 

Mensick also says, On the issue of the cannabis (sic) the applicant said that he gave as a gift to the Canadian government, I find that there is insufficient evidence that to indicate that the US federal government is seeking the applicant for flight to avoid prosecution.

First, that is a complete non-sequitur, confusing two entirely different issues. 

Second, Canada is ordering that I report to Canada Border Services Agency in Surrey so that I would have to surrender myself to the US Federal authorities on October 6.

Inasmuch as there is a felony warrant for my arrest outstanding in California, I would be taken into Federal custody at the US border because of Canada's action. I would then be held by the federal authorities for an indefinite period while arrangements were made either to return me to California, or to face federal charges of some nature, or both.

During that time, I would not be allowed to use cannabis under any circumstances, because the federal government denies that it has any medical value.

If the federal government were to decide to prosecute me on any charge, I would be held without bail or subjected to a prohibitively high bail as a flight risk. If I managed to get released on federal bail, I would be subject to frequent urine testing to be sure that I had not used cannabis. Inasmuch as I need cannabis in order to be able to urinate, that could present some problems.

Moreover, I would not be allowed even to mention anything about medical cannabis in my trial in a federal court.

I am now in the position of seeking the protection of this Court against the US Drug Enforcement Administration operating on Canadian soil, not just protection against being handed over to them at the US border.

(MarijuanaNews note: Steve needs both financial and moral support. If you can help him in any way, please contact me at cowan@MarijuanaNews.Com

Ironically, he has made major geological discoveries in BC, but they are in a private company that does not yet have funding.)

Contact numbers for Canadian officials:

Please call or email today. Please be very polite, but urge that Steve be given a fair hearing, before he is forced to return to DEAland. It might be helpful to send them the URL link to this page.)
